ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Panama Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT regime and beneficial ownership register), as amended by Law 70 of 2021; Executive Decree 129 of 2020; UAF Resolution 2020-15; Foundation Law (Law 1 of 1984) for Private Interest Foundation; Civil Procedural Law on due diligence for legal persons.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all prospective founders, directors, council members, signatories, and beneficial owners against Panamanian national PEP register (Superintendence of Banks Resolution on PEPs), the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, including a written source-of-wealth statement, approval by the compliance officer, and continuous monitoring for 12 months after commencement of business. Negative news and adverse media screening is mandatory before incorporation and at any incident-based trigger.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Certification / Panama Emprende Single Window (certificado de depósito de nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Spanish or any selected alphabet but transliterated into Spanish when used in registered documents; the statutory suffix may be 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Private Interest Foundation' or valid abbreviation; overloaded use of identical or phonetically confusing names is prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon administrative rejection, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 business days of notification, attaching a memorandum of legal precedent, a printout of the LVTS name search, and an explanation of the desired commercial identity. Thereafter, the Registro Público shall issue a final decision within 10 business days. An aggrieved party may file an amparo or contentious-administrative court action under Panamanian administrative law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible as an auxiliary administrative address for low-risk cybersecurity SaaS entities, however the mandatory statutory registered office must be a physical address in Panama maintained by a licensed resident agent. The virtual office cannot substitute the presence of a resident agent or the physical registered office address for service of process.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, Articles 1-41; supplementary provisions of the Reglamento del Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Dirección General de Registro
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Charter) inscribed in the Registro Público, accompanied by private Foundation Regulations (Reglamento)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the Founder must allocate a separate patrimony (endowment), commonly US$10,000 or the contributed asset value, which may be subscribed in cash or in kind without deposit certification prior to registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 1: (1) ENDOWMENT: The Founder's endowment of United States Dollars Ten Thousand (US$10,000.00) having been transferred, the Council accepts and subscribes same as the foundation's initial patrimony. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office in the Republic of Panama is adopted at the office of the Resident Agent, [Resident Agent], Avenida Samuel Lewis, Panama City, and such agent is ratified for all registral purposes. (3) OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed Chairman and [Name] Secretary of the Council, and [Name] is appointed Protector, each with the powers conferred by the Regulations. (4) BANKING: The Council authorizes opening bank accounts and activating Stripe payment processing, with signatories as designated. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Corporate Name (Certificado de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro (electronic certificate-of-name service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked proposed foundation names through the Public Registry's online name certificate platform and pay the official tariff. The certificate confirms that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and that it includes the word 'Foundation' or the abbreviation 'F.I.P.' as required by Law 25.
required_dossiers: Name certificate application form
Copy of the applicant's passport or corporate identity document
Statement of the three proposed names in ranked order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, select the next ranked alternate name and re-submit; if the system flags an inactive conflicting registration, file a cancellation request for that unused name or obtain a written waiver from the prior registrant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Foundation Charter and Private Regulations before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público del Circuito Judicial de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder, personally or by authorized attorney-in-fact, executes the Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado before the notary. The charter must state the foundation's name, registered office, endowment, purpose, Council members, Protector, beneficiary provisions, and amendment/dissolution rules. The private Reglamento is executed simultaneously and may remain outside the public registry. The Resident Agent signs the formal acceptance.
required_dossiers: Valid name certificate
Passport or corporate documents of the Founder
Draft Foundation Charter and draft Reglamento
Acceptance letter of the Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian lawyer or law firm)
Proof of endowment (bank wire or asset contribution statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal deficiencies, amend the draft and re-execute the deed before the same or another notary; ensure all mandatory clauses of Law 25 Article 6 are present before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized charter, registry forms, and fee receipt with the Foundation Section; upon approval the Registry issues the certified copy of the inscription (copia certificada de la inscripción). An expedited electronic filing path is available through the resident agent's licensed portal.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (first certified copy)
Registry fee payment receipt
Completed registry filing form signed by the Resident Agent
Certificate of name
Notarial protocol certificate (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any query ('razón') issued by the registry analyst within the statutory five-day window with the corrected document; failure to respond causes rejection and requires re-filing with an updated notarial certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for the Taxpayer Identification Number (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the DGI tax registration dossier to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) for the foundation, which enables invoicing, tax filings, and bank account opening. Declare the cybersecurity SaaS activities and confirm the territorial-source income treatment for services rendered to foreign clients.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
RUC registration form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
Copy of the Resident Agent's identification and accreditation
Copies of Council members' and Protector's identification for beneficial ownership disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requests clarification on declared activities or beneficial owners, file an amending form within ten business days and coordinate with the Resident Agent to harmonize RUC data with the Registry certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Municipal Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Ventanilla Única de Atención al Contribuyente / Aviso de Operación system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación, the municipal permit authorizing the foundation to carry out commercial activities from a physical address in Panama. For a fully remote SaaS operation with no physical premises, confirm with the municipality whether a domicile-only aviso or an exemption applies.
required_dossiers: RUC registration
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Lease agreement or title of the registered office premises
Copy of the Resident Agent's accreditation
Fire safety certificate of the premises (if physically occupied)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality imposes a higher tariff or requires a physical inspection, provide the lease, occupancy permit, and fire safety certificate; if the activity classification is disputed, request reclassification of the SaaS activity under the municipal tariff schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the Corporate Bank Account and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP)-licensed bank and Stripe Global Payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate KYC package to the chosen SBP-licensed bank to open a corporate account in the foundation's name for wire transfers; thereafter activate a Stripe account for card payments on the SaaS platform. The bank applies AML/KYC due diligence appropriate for a low-risk standard SaaS entity.
required_dossiers: Certified Foundation Charter and registration certificate
RUC certificate
Foundation Council Resolution No. 1 (account opening authorization)
Passports of Council members, Protector, and ultimate beneficiaries
Bank and Stripe KYC forms (source of funds, business plan, expected volumes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional evidence of legitimacy, provide SaaS service contracts, domain registration, customer invoices, and source-of-funds statements; if one bank declines, withdraw the application and re-apply to another institution with the documentation package intact.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial authority applies. The business is a cloud-based information security SaaS (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541512) and is not subject to any factory, manufacturing, or sectoral industrial license under Panamanian law; compliance is limited to the municipal Aviso de Operación and general commercial registrations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) issued by the Municipality of Panama; no separate sectoral operating license is required for cybersecurity SaaS activities under the Law 25 private interest foundation framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (low-impact, office/administrative use) under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009: filing of a Certificado de Apto Ambiental or registration through MiAMBIENTE's virtual EIA system is required only if a physical office is established; fully remote cloud SaaS operations are exempt from the full EIA process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing discharges or stack emissions arise from the SaaS activity. Office wastewater is limited to domestic sewage discharged to the municipal network per IDAAN connection permits and MiAMBIENTE discharge parameters. End-of-life IT and server hardware must be managed as e-waste under Resolución AG-0613-2018 (RAEE regulation), with disposal through a licensed recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — fire prevention certificate (visto bueno) for the registered premises, covering extinguishers, egress routes, and electrical load compliance; SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil) structural safety inspection of the leased premises; MITRADEL occupational hygiene and safety approval of the workplace in accordance with the national industrial hygiene regulation, including workstation ergonomics and electrical safety for IT equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama. Official e-services portal: SITRAN (Sistema Integrado de Tributos y Recaudaciones) at https://sitran.mef.gob.pa; DGI website: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first be registered in the Public Registry of Panama through a licensed registered agent. Tax registration procedure: (1) obtain certified copy of the foundation deed and the Public Registry inscription certificate; (2) engage a Panamanian resident agent and confirm the foundation's sworn address in Panama; (3) submit DGI Form RUC-1 (Registro Único de Contribuyente) for juridical persons, together with the certified foundation deed, resolution appointing the foundation council/representative, registered agent acceptance, passport copies of the founders/council members/beneficial owners, and proof of local address; (4) DGI will issue a RUC tax identification number and, if the foundation undertakes taxable activities, a separate ITBMS registration; (5) obtain SITRAN credentials and digital signature for electronic filing and e-invoicing. Foreign-managed PIFs may have no Panama-source income but must still maintain the annual foundation tax registration; for invoicing exports, obtaining the RUC is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available under Panamanian domestic law. A Private Interest Foundation is an entity-level juridical taxpayer and is not transparent for Panamanian tax purposes. The only relevant election is the simplified small-taxpayer regime for ITBMS, available to taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding B/.20,000, but that election does not alter entity classification or territorial-source rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.20,000 (Panamanian balboa / US dollar) annual gross income threshold for the simplified small-taxpayer regime. There is no general turnover exemption for active taxpayers: any person performing taxable transfers, providing services in Panama, or exporting goods or services must register for ITBMS before commencing operations. Foreign non-resident digital service suppliers supplying B2B or B2C services to Panama recipients may be required to register as non-resident ITBMS taxpayers even without a local permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a mandatory electronic invoicing regime under DGI Resolution 248-2020 and subsequent amendments. Registered ITBMS taxpayers must issue invoices electronically through a DGI-authorized billing operator (Proveedor de Servicios de Facturación) or through DGI's free SITRAN portal, using XML/JSON formats transmitted over SOAP/REST/API channels. Invoicing documents are cleared near-real-time by the DGI, which returns an acceptance response and generates a unique electronic validation code and QR-based digital stamp. Forged, uncleared, or non-validated invoices are inadmissible for the buyer's ITBMS credit and expose the seller to fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT/ITBMS rate may be claimed on (a) goods physically exported from Panama under a valid export customs declaration, and (b) services provided to non-resident clients where the service is rendered or economically exploited outside Panama. For a Panama-based PIF providing cybersecurity SaaS vulnerability scanning and penetration testing, the zero-rating criteria are: the client is not domiciled or resident in Panama; the service is initiated from Panama infrastructure but is used, consumed, and economically benefited offshore; there is a written contract evidencing offshore supply; the invoice is marked as an export/zero-rated transaction; and payment is received from a foreign bank account or remittance channel. The zero-rated income must be reported in the monthly ITBMS return, and input VAT attributable to the export activity may be credited or refunded to the PIF.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaración Única de Aduana) for goods; for pure services, a formal export declaration is generally replaced by a notarized service contract and delivery/acceptance certificate
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or electronic equivalent evidencing physical departure for goods, or for services, a signed service-completion and remote-delivery certificate
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank credit advice confirming payment from the non-resident client outside Panama
Residence/registration certificate or tax ID of the offshore customer and an explicit description of the offshore beneficial use of the SaaS service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims for the general tax prescription period of five years (extended to ten years for non-declared or fraudulent filings). If documentation is deficient or the arrangement is deemed false or artificial, the DGI will reverse the zero rate, retroactively charge 7% ITBMS on the gross export sales, add monthly surcharges capped at 100% of the tax, impose legal interest, and apply fines typically ranging from 25% to 200% of the omitted tax. Fraudulent export claims involving forged customs documents, false beneficiary declarations, or sham non-resident transactions are additionally subject to criminal tax fraud penalties under Panamanian law (Law 76 of 2019 and the Criminal-Corporate regime), including imprisonment from two to six years, suspension of the exporter's RUC/ITBMS registration, and disqualification from future export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the sole banking and trust supervisory authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá functions as fiscal and clearing agent under Law 44 of 1975. Panama has no conventional central bank and no foreign-exchange administration office; the monetary regime is full dollarization (USD unlimited legal tender since 1904, with the Balboa/PAB circulating only as 1:1 coins), so monetary and FX policy is effectively conducted by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the AML/CFT intelligence unit receiving transactional reports.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There is no exchange-control law, no Central Bank permit gate, no conversion queue, and no restriction on holding, converting, or remitting foreign currency. PAB is redeemable at a fixed 1:1 rate with USD, which removes any currency drift within Panama. Cross-border profit remittance by a Private Interest Foundation is legally unrestricted; the only practical hurdles are commercial bank CDD, UAF reporting of transactions above USD 10,000, and OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening by U.S. correspondent banks. Under the territorial tax system (Código Fiscal Arts. 694-695 and Law 52 of 2012), foreign-source income of the PIF is excluded from Panamanian income tax, and distributions of such income to beneficiaries do not trigger Panamanian dividend withholding provided the PIF did not carry on a trade or business within Panamanian territory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory timeline for surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts, whether goods or services. SaaS penetration-testing and vulnerability-scanning subscription revenue (ISIC 6201) is treated as a service export; proceeds freely accrue in USD and may remain indefinitely in domestic USD accounts. No export license is required for this scope. The sole compliance obligations on receipt are (i) bank verification of the commercial invoice supporting the wire, (ii) UAF cash-transaction reporting for currency-based operations above USD 10,000, and (iii) SBP Acuerdo 01-2014 record-keeping for customer due diligence. Territorial taxation means such foreign-source service revenue is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax, but the bank file must prove that the services were performed or contractually sourced outside Panama.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury account; MEDIUM only as a narrow pass-through collection rail for SaaS card settlements. Legal constraints: Panama does not maintain an EMI or digital-bank license class; the SBP grants only general or international banking licenses under Decree Law 2 of 2008, and deposit-taking by an unlicensed entity is unlawful. Major offshore EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury) do not accept Panama-domiciled Private Interest Foundations in their eligible-jurisdiction lists, and a foundation is not a natural counterparty for their CDD. The compliant architecture is a two-entity structure: (1) a U.S. Delaware C-Corp as the operating company owns the Stripe account and receives subscription settlements; (2) surplus profits are distributed or contributed to the Panama PIF via SWIFT as foreign-source funds, supported by intercompany contracts and invoices. If a U.S. EMI is used as a settlement account, it must be held by the U.S. operating entity only, with same-day onward transfer to the SBP-licensed Panamanian bank; no Panama-regulated activity is then triggered.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SBP Acuerdo 01-2014 as amended, each bank must identify the foundation, its Foundation Council members, and every beneficial owner holding 10% or more of the foundation's assets or voting rights. A documented in-person identity interview is mandatory for the ultimate beneficial owner and at least the founding council member; remote opening is permitted only as a two-step hybrid procedure: (i) a live video interview before the bank's compliance officer with prior apostilled identity documents, and (ii) original notarized and apostilled signature pages plus a certificate of existence (personería jurídica) issued by the Registro Público de Panamá, delivered through a licensed Panamanian law firm with a standing relationship with the bank. A power of attorney may substitute for physical appearance only for administration of funds, not for the foundational interview of the beneficial owner. Towerbank and Banco General private-banking desks have the most repeatable remote-boarding protocol for reputable PIFs; the pragmatic recommendation is that the principal beneficial owner appears once in Panama City to complete onboarding, thereafter all instructions flow by POA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or opaque foundation structure: bank perceives use of third-party council members or a 'shell' registered agent files, flashing red flags under Acuerdo 01-2014 and FATF Recommendation 24
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered foundation deed (Acta Constitutiva) recorded at Registro Público; statutory schedule of beneficiaries and council members attached to the deed; sworn declaration that no undisclosed beneficiaries exist; Panamanian counsel legal opinion confirming the PIF's validity and the lawful purpose of asset holding; current certificate of good standing; registered-agent engagement letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Short operating history and digital SaaS revenue pattern: bank flags a newly formed PIF receiving recurring subscription wires from cloud payment processors without underlying business substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and three-year projections for the cloud vulnerability scanning platform; executed SaaS license and penetration-testing master agreements with named clients; payment-processor settlement statements (Stripe, Wire Transfer) evidencing end-customer flows; audited or reviewed financial statements; evidence of economic substance (office address, council minutes, foreign contract file).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cybersecurity end-user and defense-sector concerns: penetration-testing tooling may be perceived as dual-use or as serving sanctioned clients, triggering sanctions-enhanced due diligence and refusal of correspondent banking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product classification memo mapping the software to ISIC 6201/NAICS 541512; demonstrable absence of export-restricted functionality; OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions-screening results for all beneficial owners and clients; SOC 2 Type II attestation; end-user attestation letters; refusal of work with military or government entities in sanctioned jurisdictions where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Divergent or high-frequency transaction pattern: frequent inbound liquidity followed by rapid outbound distributions may be treated as money-laundering layering by the bank's transaction-monitoring engine
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and Foundation Council resolutions authorizing treasury policies; matched commercial invoices and MT103 beneficiary references for every wire; an internal treasury ledger mapping each receipt to its corresponding disbursement rationale; audit trail of intellectual-property licensing between the operating entity and the PIF; auditor's written comfort on intercompany balances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the foundation's initial endowment fund (minimum B/.10,000 equivalent per Ley 25 of 1995, payable in installments or in kind) is a SWIFT MT103 from the founder's account with purpose code 'CAP' (capital contribution) or 'GIFT' (settlor's gift) and narrative 'Aporte Fundacional — Private Interest Foundation Endowment'. The receiving account is the PIF's named USD account at the SBP-licensed bank, and the beneficiary name must match exactly the foundation name recorded at the Registro Público. The KYC file requires the registered foundation deed, certificate of good standing, passport pages of the settlor and council members, and a source-of-wealth statement for the injected funds. For ongoing surplus distribution from the U.S. SaaS operating company, use MT103 with narrative 'Foreign-source profit distribution under operating agreement', supported by an intercompany services agreement and profit-allocation schedule; do not characterize recurrent injections as loans to the PIF because the foundation cannot operate as a commercial borrower without triggering Panamanian-source characterization. Verification is performed via SWIFT GPI end-to-end tracking and the bank's credit-instruction letter confirming the exact project reference. All incoming wires above USD 10,000 are reported to the UAF under the mandatory currency-transaction reporting threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound clearing rail for SaaS trade settlement is SWIFT MT103 (General Purpose / cover to correspondent), executed from the Panamanian foundation's USD account to supplier or licensee accounts, with each payment tied to the corresponding commercial invoice, ISIC 6201 service description, and the foundation's audited treasury ledger. For high-value cybersecurity hardware procurement (above USD 250,000, e.g., scanning appliances or infrastructure), a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by the Panamanian bank with a U.S. advising bank is permissible but not generally necessary for pure SaaS delivery; documentary collection (MT400) is the intermediate option. Domestic vendor payments clear through the Banco Nacional de Panamá clearing house in USD with no FX step since PAB is pegged 1:1. Every outbound wire above USD 10,000 must name the ultimate beneficiary and include the invoice number, and the foundation's council must minute-approve recurring disbursements to prevent the bank's autonomous transaction-monitoring from flagging layering.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable currency forwards arranged via the international trading desks of SBP-licensed banks for EU/UK SaaS license revenues
USD/BRL, USD/COP, and USD/CLP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for Latin American enterprise subscription receivables
EUR-USD cross-currency basis swaps to hedge cloud-supplier costs denominated in EUR
FX spot conversion executed within SWIFT MT103 settlement for immediate disbursements
Zero-cost collar and risk-reversal structures on LatAm currencies for large recurring licensing contracts
USD interest-rate and liquidity management is not required at the PAB level because USD is legal tender and PAB is a pure 1:1 coin representation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foundation franchise fee (annual government fee / impuesto de franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Registry of Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on January 15; late payment permitted through March 31 with graduated penalties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 50 surcharge if paid in February, USD 100 surge if paid in March; after March 31, an additional penalty of 10% plus monthly legal interest accrues. Failure to pay for two consecutive years can trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution of the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual aggregate beneficial owner confirmation (UBO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI) – Electronic Beneficial Ownership Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for existing foundations; any transfer of foundation rights or shares must be updated within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 100 to USD 10,000 per infraction; repeated or deliberate non-filing can result in suspension of the foundation's legal capacity and legal personality.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a private interest foundation solely by virtue of its status. A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the foundation conducts taxable commercial activity in Panama with annual gross revenue exceeding USD 3,000,000, or if it is licensed as a financial, insurance, securities, or trust entity. PIF charters may also contractually require an annual audit for the protection of beneficiaries.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Foundations subject to Panamanian tax obligations must maintain accounting records on an accrual basis in conformity with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities, as applicable to their size. Purely passive foundations may keep simplified internal records consistent with the foundation charter, provided the books are sufficient to verify assets and movements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent maintains a private beneficial ownership register at the registered office. Annually, the agent must file with DGI the complete list of founders, council members, and any natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control the foundation. Every transfer of foundation rights or shares during the prior year must be recorded and reported to DGI within 30 days; a signed confirmation is placed in the statutory minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Founders) and Transfer of Rights
Register of Council Members (Directors) and Secretary
Minute Book of Annual and Special Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 8,000 per year (only when audit threshold is met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000; 15% on the first USD 1,500,000 of taxable income (Law 8 of 2010, Fiscal Code Article 733). Because Panama applies territorial taxation, the effective rate on purely foreign-source cybersecurity SaaS revenue is 0% when the services are rendered and consumed outside Panama.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source rule: only Panamanian-source income is taxed. No general tax holiday, no patent box, and the former 0% royalty exemption for IP exploitation was repealed effective FY2020. Structurally, a Private Interest Foundation derives no Panamanian tax on foreign-source subscriptions; the only fixed annual burden is the USD 300 PIF franchise fee. ITBMS (7% VAT equivalent) does not apply to exported digital services.
